description: Team Echelon is a group of students passionate about technology, engineering, and solving real-world problems. We bring different skills and perspectives together, with a shared interest in learning, building, and creating practical solutions. As participants in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, we look forward to exploring new ideas, working together, and contributing to solutions for challenges in space exploration.
summary:
IGNIS (Intelligent Guidance and NASA-Informed Safety System) is a platform that helps people find, understand, analyse, and compare research on how fire behaves in space.

We developed a web application that brings microgravity combustion research into one place. Users can explore different experiments, view their conditions and results, analyze available data, compare findings, and ask questions about the research using an AI assistant.

IGNIS addresses the NASA Flame in Freefall challenge by making it easier to work with research data that can otherwise be difficult to find, compare, and understand.

This is important because fire behaves differently in space than it does on Earth. Understanding these differences can help researchers learn more about fire in microgravity and contribute to improving fire safety for astronauts and future space missions.
details:
IGNIS (Intelligent Guidance and NASA-Informed Safety System) is a web platform developed to make research on fire behaviour in microgravity easier to access and understand.

The platform allows users to explore different microgravity combustion experiments, view experimental conditions and available results, analyze data, and compare findings across investigations. It also includes an AI-powered assistant that helps users ask questions and understand information related to the research.

IGNIS works by organizing available research data into a single platform. Users can search through the experiments, select the information they need, explore the available data through visualizations, and use the assistant to get explanations based on the research information provided to it.

The project can save researchers time and make it easier for students, scientists, and other interested users to work with microgravity combustion research. Its intended impact is to support a better understanding of how fire behaves in space and contribute to research that can improve fire safety for astronauts and future space missions.

We developed IGNIS using React and TypeScript for the frontend, Node.js and Express for the backend, and Google's Gemini API for the AI assistant. We also used structured microgravity combustion research data to build the platform. No special hardware was required.

What makes IGNIS creative is that it brings research exploration, data analysis, experiment comparison, and AI-assisted explanations together in one platform. Rather than simply providing links to research papers, it helps users interact with the available information.

During development, our team considered the accuracy of scientific information, the quality and availability of the data, ease of use, accessibility, and the limitations of the available research. We also considered the importance of ensuring that AI-generated explanations are checked against the original scientific evidence.
